quarterly_data.signal: CALL (verbatim) — RECURRING METRICS, CFO Mark Patterson: total RPO was $46.7 billion, up 7%, with product RPO up 9%; total ARR ended the quarter at $32.1 billion, up 3%, with product ARR growth of 5%; total subscription revenue represented 48% of Cisco's total revenue; total software revenue was $6.2 billion, up 11%.
quarterly_data.figure: RPO $46.7B (+7%), product RPO +9%; ARR $32.1B (+3%); software revenue $6.2B (+11%); subscription 48% of revenue

quarterly_data.signal: CALL (verbatim) — FY2027 SHAPE AND AI BACKLOG, CFO Mark Patterson: the Q1 revenue guide is 'at about 25% of the year, and our three-year average is for Q1 to be about 25%'; for Q2 through Q4 'the implied growth is more like 13%' as comps get much tougher, and 'we are being prudent on the remainder of the year'. On the $7.5 billion of AI hyperscale revenue: 'you should sort of expect a good trend line in terms of gradual increases as we move from Q1 through Q4.' On AI orders versus revenue: 'we did about $4 billion in revenue and $9 billion in orders for FY 2026. So obviously you are entering with some good backlog as we go into 2027. But these are non-linear orders that are massive in scale and are usually placed well ahead of time. So I think the $7.5 billion is a good prudent guide for the year.'
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 guide ~25% of FY2027; Q2-Q4 implied ~13%; FY2026 AI ~$4B revenue vs $9B orders

quarterly_data.signal: CALL (verbatim) — HYPERSCALER AND TELCO DEMAND, CEO Chuck Robbins: 'at the beginning of the quarter, we said we would do over $4 billion and we did over $4 billion, which was obviously the largest quarter of the year for us', and 'I don't think there's been any change at all in the material demand from our hyperscaler customers.' Telcos are getting 'the inbounds from these customers talking about their need for bandwidth, and that's what's leading them to spend' on AI workloads and scale-across. In closing, the CEO said that just over six years ago Cisco 'had virtually no business with them inside their data centers'; through investments and acquisitions in silicon, optics and security it rebuilt those hyperscaler relationships, offering to sell 'silicon software or systems or any combination of those'.
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 hyperscale AI orders over $4B, as guided at the start of the quarter

quarterly_data.signal: CALL (verbatim) — LEAD TIMES AND MERCHANT SILICON, CFO Mark Patterson: 'not seeing any significant lead time issues at all. I think we've got some tightness, obviously, in some parts of the supply chain. I'm not sure I would even say constraints', and 'I'm not hearing any escalations from customers on lead time issues'. Dealing directly with TSMC, 'we're not waiting on any sort of allocation and commits and decommits, if you will, from any merchant silicon providers'; 'in out years, you're going to see, obviously, I think some avoidance of stacking margins with merchant silicon as well, but that's kind of down the road just a little bit.'

CALL (verbatim) — SECURITY, SPLUNK AND COLLABORATION. CFO Mark Patterson: the 14% Q4 security revenue growth 'did have a little bit of an anomaly in there' — 'sizable on-prem deals that also had a little bit longer duration' at Splunk 'significantly helped the overall security number'; longer term the mix is 'likely going back to more of a 2/3 in the cloud, 1/3 on-prem', and 'security is probably mid-to-high single digits in Q1 and improving as we go through the year.' CEO Chuck Robbins: over 1,500 customers bought the new security products (Secure Access, XDR, Hypershield, AI Defense) in Q4 (he cited 1,600 new customers in Q&A), bringing net new customers to over 6,400 since launch; firewall orders grew over 30% in Q4, 'a second quarter in a row of 30% growth'; the organic Cisco security solutions were 'high single digits' exiting the year. Splunk added more than 280 new logos in Q4 and Cisco exceeded its target of 1,000 new Splunk logos for the year. Collaboration had its best quarterly performance in seven years, with video devices growing 40% year-over-year.
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 security revenue +14% (on-prem Splunk deals); >6,400 new-product security customers since launch; firewall orders +30%; Splunk >280 new logos

quarterly_data.signal: CALL (verbatim) — ENTERPRISE WINS AND REFRESH, CEO Chuck Robbins: 'a leading U.S. global bank placed an order for 1,000 Cisco Data Center Smart Switches, replacing a major networking competitor and a major firewall competitor', and 'A leading frontier AI company has chosen Cisco's campus networking solution, including Wi-Fi 7 access points, smart switches, and end-to-end segmentation'. On enterprise AI deployment: 'If they move to open-weight models or models that they are running on-prem, that is great for us because it means they will invest in more enterprise private data center networking'. On the refresh: 'We have got 8,000 or 9,000 customers running Cisco IQ today that are actually assessing their infrastructure', and 'our competitor's last day of support is also a market opportunity for us' — a major U.S. manufacturer wanted Cisco to replace a competitor's gear that was past last day of support on its manufacturing floors.
quarterly_data.figure: 1,000 Data Center Smart Switches ordered by a U.S. global bank; 8,000-9,000 customers running Cisco IQ

quarterly_data.signal: CALL (verbatim) — SOFTWARE AND AI TOOLS, CEO Chuck Robbins: since its launch at Cisco Live U.S. in June, 'nearly 4,500 enterprises have signed up for Cisco Cloud Control'; Cisco launched Antares, 'a family of open-weight small language models designed to help cybersecurity professionals pinpoint known vulnerabilities within a code base'; Resilient Infrastructure Services, powered by Cisco IQ, 'now has over 8,600 customers'. Internally, 'In FY 2026, 145,000 support cases were resolved entirely by AI with zero human intervention', and the Circuit on-prem AI assistant supported 'over 75 million prompts in Q4'.
quarterly_data.figure: Cisco Cloud Control ~4,500 enterprises signed up; Resilient Infrastructure Services >8,600 customers; 145,000 support cases resolved by AI
